best_parts: node shock_t31a: tempting-then-refute feedback ('It is tempting because burns do get infected... in the first hours the plasma leak comes first') with a sure_note
node depth_t18: names the wrong model implicitly, refutes with the colour/blanching/refill signs, offers 'Show me why' deeper lane
node depth2: contrast probe re-tests TR18 in a different form (feature separation) after the vignette, as the trap map asks
flaws: node depth: only one distractor (Full thickness, TR18); a learner holding the superficial-partial model cannot be diagnosed here, and the probe is close to a yes/no
node depth2_ok: the key ('Dry, leathery, insensate, and does not blanch') is the longest of the three options, so the key is findable by form (DP1)
node mech: stem 'The heart is somewhat depressed too, so the pump can look like the problem' pre-loads the inotrope answer and gives away part of the reasoning before the probe
O4 'with and without colloid' is never probed in S3: the colloid rule appears only in mech_t8 feedback, so a learner can finish the segment without committing to it
no fast lane and no 'Why?' agency on the correct paths; a confident expert and a guessing novice get the same path

best_parts: node cold_check: four options that each change exactly one component (shock type, depth, fluid, colloid), so the learner must check all three and no wrong option is dominated; a clean recombination probe

nodes shock_septic and shock_cardio plus their _why explain nodes: each names the wrong model, says why it tempts ('burns do depress the heart a little'), and refutes it with the haematocrit and urine clues

chain fluid_t8 -> colloid_probe -> formula_probe -> formula_t8: colloid timing and the Parkland-versus-Evans pair are both probed, covering the 'with and without colloid' objective the other variants skip
flaws: node colloid_probe and formula_probe: two-option binary probes (one trap plus the key), so the trap is not comparably tempting and the learner cannot be diagnosed beyond yes or no
node depth_case: binary (full thickness versus deep partial); the superficial look-alike used in other variants is missing here
node cold_check: the correct option is the longest of the four, so the key is partly findable by form (DP1)
node fluid_probe: the correct option 'Titrated Ringer lactate, guided by urine output' is the longest of the four (DP1)
segment length: seven probes for one segment is a heavy load at 1 a.m.; several probes repeat the same yes-or-no pattern, and 'Yes.' opens most feedback nodes, which feels mechanical

best_parts: node depth: three options with two different traps (full thickness, superficial partial) and the key, so the learner's specific wrong belief shows up; depth_t_sup correctly names the tempting 'shallower step' read

node contrast_t_pain: names the tempting separator ('Pain is the first thing you check at the bedside, so it feels like the separator') and refutes it with the insensate sign; the correct option is not the longest (DP1 clean)
node case_ok: 'Why does plasma leak so fast?' offers a deeper lane on a correct pick, with case_why giving the mechanism; agency that a learner can choose
flaws: node final: the only option with a number ('48 to 72 hours') is the key, so the key is findable by form (DP1); the 'Septic shock first, so antibiotics before fluid' option is weaker than the other three and is dominated
node tbsa_note: 'TBSA' appears without expansion on first use (DP25), and the node tells the learner the erythema rule without a probe
node mech: a single-question probe with one trap (inotropes) plus albumin; the first-line fluid is not contrasted with the Evans formula, so the colloid objective is only partly probed
no fast lane for experts; the 'Show me why' deeper option is offered only on the correct case_ok and not on the trap nodes depth_t_full or case_t_sep

merge_ideas: b's cold_check recombination (one-component-changed options) plus c's three-option depth probe with the superficial-partial look-alike, so the depth probe is not binary
c's contrast_t_pain wording ('Pain is the first thing you check... so it feels like the separator') with b's named-model feedback, which together make the tempting belief explicit
a's compact shock feedback and its single-question probes as the core, with b's colloid and formula chain added only where the colloid objective needs it, to cut b's seven-probe load
add a fast lane to the shock probe (correct and sure: skip to cold_check) and a 'Why?' deeper option on the correct paths of a, b and c, so experts and novices diverge
rewrite the key of c's final probe and b's cold_check so the key is not the only longest or only numeric option
